summary: Unelected New York parks chief Robert Moses reshaped the city and state from the 1920s to 1962, building car-centred highways and parks that displaced Black neighbourhoods, blocked transit and walled off the poor.

evidence.note: born in New Haven, Connecticut, in 1888 to an affluent Jewish family
Yale quota on Jewish students shapes his position on the edge of elite society
extended segment on his Egypt visit and admiration for British colonial rule under Kitchener
first city job in civil service reform against Tammany Hall patronage
made head of Long Island and state park bodies in the 1920s, holds them about forty years
low bridges and vetoed rail line keep buses and poor, Black visitors from Jones Beach
Cross Bronx Expressway evicts mostly Black residents of East Tremont
displaced tenants pushed into crowded tenements; housing inequality
playground and park spending in Harlem far below white neighbourhoods
stripped of most offices in 1962 when Rockefeller accepts his resignation
dies in 1981; subway decay and MTA plans followed up to recent years

notes: No theme for urban planning, infrastructure or public transit, the story's real core; racism-white-supremacy chosen as closest (racist housing and segregation). Main_span start 1924 is from general knowledge (transcript says early 1920s).
